title: Tissue Traction Assessment Study: Reliability and Comparative Assessment of Skin and Soft-Tissue Mobility and Pain Sensitivity in Scarred and Contralateral Non-Scarred Tissue
summary:
Scars resulting from surgery or injuries may change how easily the skin and underlying tissues move and how sensitive they are to pressure or stretching. Different devices are available to assess these properties, but it is not yet clear how consistently they produce measurements when used by different examiners.

This study aims to compare these measurement methods and determine how reliably they assess skin mobility and pain sensitivity.

Forty adults aged 18–75 years with a healed scar of at least 2 cm on one side of the body will participate. Each participant will attend one examination session.

Measurements will be performed at five locations: the scar, the corresponding scar-free area on the opposite side, the forearm, the upper pelvic region, and the lower back.

Several non-invasive devices will be used to assess skin movement and mechanical properties. Pressure and skin stretching will also be applied gradually to identify when participants first experience pain. Ultrasound will be used at one location on the lower back.

Two examiners will perform repeated measurements to assess the consistency of the results. Participants will also complete a questionnaire about their scar, and a photograph of the scar will be taken.

No treatment will be provided. Some measurements may cause brief discomfort, and participants may pause or stop at any time.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Presence of a unilateral, healed surgical or injury-related scar with a visible length of at least 2 cm.
2. An anatomically comparable mirror region on the contralateral side of the body must be identifiable and free of visible scars or comparable previous injury.
3. Wound healing must be sufficiently advanced or complete to allow non-invasive mechanical measurements without difficulty. No minimum scar age in months is required.
4. Skin at the intended measurement sites must be intact and suitable for assessment.
5. Ability to understand the study procedures, follow measurement instructions, and provide written informed consent.
6. Ability to maintain the required standardized body positions during the measurements.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Open wounds, incomplete wound healing, active bleeding, or ulceration at the intended measurement sites.
2. Acute local inflammation, infection, or active dermatological disease that could interfere with the measurements or increase participant risk.
3. Absence of an anatomically comparable scar-free contralateral control region.
4. Known allergy or intolerance to skin adhesives, temporary skin-marking materials, or other materials required for the measurements.
5. Inability to tolerate the standardized measurement positions or procedures.
6. Any medical or other condition that, in the investigator's judgement, makes participation or the planned non-invasive measurements unsuitable or unsafe.
